clue.text: O, Willie! Mr T's on! What a beano! Could this be a wealth-creation programme?

annotation.answer: WHO WANTS TO BE A MILLIONAIRE

indicators.note: a beano is a riotous party, so the words before it are thrown into a wild jumble

blocks.clueFragment: O, Willie! Mr T's on! What a beano
blocks.note: every letter of the exclamations, including 'What a beano' itself, is the fodder, plus one I the printed words lack

explanation.surface: Someone cheers excitedly as Mr T comes on, wondering if this is a show about making money.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: the fodder has 23 letters with only two Is, while WHO WANTS TO BE A MILLIONAIRE has 24 with three Is, so one I is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ITV quiz show offered contestants a top prize of one million pounds, so it is a programme that creates wealth.

clue.text: Sound of a mighty theatre organ: it's going like a dervish

definitions.note: a clause describing the thing rather than a plain noun

blocks.clueFragment: Sound of a mighty theatre organ
blocks.note: the Wurlitzer was the famous mighty cinema and theatre organ; its opening sounds like this word

explanation.surface: A huge theatre organ roars so loudly the whole place seems to spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: only the start of Wurlitzer, the organ maker's name, is heard in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish spins round and round in a Sufi dance, so anything spinning that way is one that whirls.

clue.text: Polyphemus was like a god to Mad Carew

definitions.text: like a god to Mad Carew

blocks.note: first meaning: Polyphemus was the Cyclops of the Odyssey, with a single eye

blocks.clueFragment: like a god to Mad Carew
blocks.note: second meaning: in the poem The Green Eye of the Yellow God, Mad Carew robs an idol with one eye

explanation.walkthrough: J. Milton Hayes's monologue opens with a one-eyed yellow idol north of Khatmandu, whose emerald eye Mad Carew steals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Cyclops and the poem's idol have just a single eye, which is exactly what the compound adjective describes.

clue.text: No one left to strike in this conflict?

definitions.text: No one left to strike in this conflict?

blocks.note: when every worker has walked out, or a cricket side is all out, nobody remains to strike
a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: A dispute so total that every last worker has already downed tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: total war leaves nobody uncommitted, like a strike with everyone already out.
explanation.definitionFit: Total warfare commits every available force and resource, holding nothing back from the fighting.

clue.text: Figure worshipped in a Shinto temple

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: the end of Shinto runs on into the start of temple

explanation.surface: An idol venerated at a Japanese shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblematic object or figure, often carved, revered as a clan's sacred symbol.

clue.text: Saint seeking neurosurgery on Cadfael's patch

indicators.note: surgery is an operation, so the letters beside it are cut and rearranged

blocks.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for saint
the word splits in two: its first part is the fodder, the rest is the operation performed on it

explanation.surface: A holy man looks for brain surgery on the monk detective's bald spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Neurosurgery splits: 'neuro' is fodder and 'surgery' operates on it. Brother Cadfael is Ellis Peters's medieval monk sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's shaved crown is the bald patch left by clerical shaving, worn by Benedictines like Cadfael.

clue.text: Sand-dune to obstruct a Mongol ruler

blocks.note: to bar is to block or obstruct
a khan was a Mongol ruler, as in Genghis Khan

explanation.surface: A sandbank in the desert halts the progress of a Mongol chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A barkhan is a crescent-shaped dune formed by wind in deserts, a technical geographical term.

clue.text: Misspent youth! Hereon we use mono-construction to give practical backing

annotation.answer: PUT ONE'S MONEY WHERE ONE'S MOUTH IS

indicators.note: a construction is something built, so the preceding letters are assembled into a new form

blocks.clueFragment: Misspent youth! Hereon we use mono-
blocks.note: all twenty-eight letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a wasted youth and vows to build only in mono from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misspent' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; the signal is 'construction'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to back up one's words with action, especially by staking cash on a claim.

clue.text: Less than perfect trade agreement from seat of learning

blocks.note: UNI is short for university
a deal is a business bargain

explanation.surface: A flawed commercial contract signed by a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something falling short of the ideal is imperfect or not quite optimal.

clue.text: Disraeli's Christian hero bitterly recanted out East

indicators.note: 'out' says the following letter is removed
done bitterly, in anguish, the word is twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A Christian protagonist travelling in the Orient bitterly renounces his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is dropped from recanted and the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tancred, or The New Crusade is an 1847 novel by Disraeli whose young nobleman goes to the Holy Land.

clue.text: Eyesore from Hell, like a rare and classical mess

indicators.note: a mess is a disordered jumble, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld, or Hell
as means like
taken as written
ET is Latin for and

explanation.surface: An ugly sight is likened to Hell and a rare old classical shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' signals Latin, so 'and' becomes ET before joining the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A place so ruined or squalid that it seems wrecked by catastrophe, used loosely for any blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Platters hit the sole surviving solver

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1955 hit record by the American vocal group The Platters
second meaning: the person addressed, the solver, as the one left

explanation.walkthrough: 'Platters' looks like dishes being struck; it is the doo-wop group, and the solver is addressed as 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title and a phrase saying nobody remains except the person being addressed by the clue.

clue.text: See 7
Red Queen swapped places and proved she was human?

definitions.note: a clause; the answer is a past-tense verb meaning made a mistake

indicators.note: the two words exchange positions, so they are joined in the reverse of clue order

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Red Queen of Through the Looking-Glass shifted position and showed a human failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To err is human', so making a mistake proves one is human.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'to err is human' makes committing a mistake the mark of being only mortal.

clue.text: See 7
Issue voiced from the Miss Woodhouse country

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so we go by how the following words are said

blocks.note: Emma Woodhouse is Jane Austen's heroine and a country is a nation

explanation.surface: Something said in the land of Austen's matchmaking heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or flows out from a source, so the noun issue fits.

clue.text: Whence Condon's candidate had hardhearted man at papal court

indicators.note: to be hearted is to be given a heart, so a letter goes into the middle of the word that holds it

blocks.note: taken as written
the word splits in two: hard is H, as on a pencil, and the rest says where it goes
the Curia is the papal court of the Vatican

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted man at the Vatican linked to the novelist's brainwashed candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardhearted' splits into hard, giving H, and hearted, which puts it inside the court.
explanation.definitionFit: In Richard Condon's thriller The Manchurian Candidate, the brainwashed soldier is conditioned in that region of northeast China.

clue.text: Specious specific in no way unusual

blocks.note: taken as written
ST, street, is a way
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A dubious cure that is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: A specific is an old word for a remedy aimed at a particular illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine of doubtful worth, sold as a sure cure by its promoter.

clue.text: The grip of the omnium-gatherum?

blocks.note: first meaning: a grip is an old word for a travelling bag
second meaning: a miscellaneous collection that takes in everything

explanation.walkthrough: 'The grip of' reads like a firm hold; grip is in fact a bag, and the answer, read as two words, describes a collection of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A large soft travel bag carries all kinds of belongings, and literally it 'holds all', like a miscellany.

clue.text: Solecism committed with fawning affectation

indicators.note: 'with' read as within, the letters are found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of fawning runs into the start of affectation

explanation.surface: A social blunder made through obsequious pretension.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a breach of etiquette or grammar, just as a faux pas or blunder is.

clue.text: Soundly criticise Italy's dumplings

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so what follows is heard rather than read

blocks.note: to knock is to criticise, and I is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone firmly condemns Italian dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works only with the anglicised 'nocky', not the Italian 'nyokki'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato, semolina or flour.

clue.text: Trimming shortened measure in a pint

indicators.note: shortened says the phrase is cut down to its abbreviated form

blocks.note: an imperial pint holds twenty of these liquid measures

explanation.surface: Cutting back on the beer by a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: Fluid ounce is abbreviated fl oz, so shortening the first word leaves FL before OUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounce is a gathered frill sewn on a skirt or curtain as decorative edging.

clue.text: Space executive left one's monkey in this

definitions.note: points to the genus that holds the monkey rather than naming it

blocks.note: NASA is the US space agency, an executive agency of government
L is the abbreviation for left
one is, written as I plus is

explanation.surface: An agency chief abandoned his monkey here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasalis is the zoological genus containing the proboscis monkey of Borneo, named for its long nose.

clue.text: Doubtful Greek character: mother's raising another!

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upward, so it is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ma is mother, plus the possessive s
another Greek character, the letter pi

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy Greek, whose mother is bringing up a second child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampi is an archaic Greek letter used only as a numeral for 900, of uncertain origin and name.

clue.text: A Moor's downfall a fallen woman?

indicators.note: a downfall is a collapse, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Othello's ruin was a woman thought to be unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' doubles as the last letter and part of the definition: a word for a wanton woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorosa is an archaic loan word for a wanton or amorous woman, a courtesan.

clue.text: Main offenders suspended from this branch of the Met?

definitions.note: a clause pointing to the spar rather than a plain noun

blocks.note: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police
an arm is a branch or division

explanation.surface: Criminals hanged by a division of London's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, the Spanish Main, so the offenders are pirates hanged from a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates and mutineers were traditionally hanged from the end of the spar crossing a ship's mast.

clue.text: Holy smoke!

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclamation of surprise
setter's reading: the fragrant fumes burned in church

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it an expression of shock; read literally it is the sweet smoke of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic resin burned during religious rites gives off sacred fumes in a thurible.

clue.text: See 1
